cards.q: What is the first thing a driver should think about when arriving at a road accident?
cards.a: Securing safety at the scene so that no further danger arises.

cards.q: Should you always run straight to the injured as soon as you reach an accident?
cards.a: No. First assess the situation and secure safety at the scene.

cards.q: Why must the scene of an accident be secured?
cards.a: To prevent further accidents and danger to the injured, to helpers and to other road users.

cards.q: What is the emergency number in Iceland?
What information is important to give when calling 112?
cards.a: Where the accident is, what happened, how many may be injured and what dangers are at the scene.

cards.q: Should an injured person be moved out of the vehicle straight away?
cards.a: No, unless particular necessity requires it, for example because of imminent danger.

cards.q: What can count as imminent danger at the scene of an accident?
cards.a: For example fire, smoke or the risk of a further collision.

cards.q: What should be done if a person is bleeding heavily?
cards.a: Apply direct pressure to the bleeding wound and call for help.

cards.q: What should be done if a person is unconscious?
cards.a: Check their breathing and make sure the airway is open.

cards.q: What should be done if a person is not breathing normally?
cards.a: Call 112 and start CPR according to the instructions.

cards.q: What should be done if an unconscious person is breathing normally?
cards.a: Secure the airway, monitor their breathing and place them in the recovery position when appropriate.

cards.q: Should an injured person be given food or drink after a serious accident?
cards.a: No, in general injured people should not be given food or drink.

cards.q: What should a driver keep in mind before getting out of the car after an accident?
cards.a: The traffic and other hazards at the scene.

cards.q: What must be done if there is a risk of other vehicles driving into the scene?
cards.a: Warn other road users and secure the scene as far as possible.

cards.q: Is it right to move an injured person out of the car if the car is in danger of catching fire?
cards.a: Yes, if it is necessary to rescue the person from imminent danger.

cards.q: Why is it important to follow the instructions of 112?
cards.a: Emergency operators can advise on the right response until professionals arrive.

cards.q: May a driver leave the scene of an accident without checking whether help is needed?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What should be done if you are unsure about the condition of an injured person?
cards.a: Call 112 and follow the instructions of the emergency operator.

cards.q: Which is more important: starting first aid straight away or making sure the scene is not dangerous?
cards.a: First the situation must be secured so that no further danger arises, unless imminent danger calls for immediate action.

cards.q: May a helmet be removed from an injured motorcyclist unnecessarily?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What should be done if an injured person is trapped in a vehicle?
cards.a: Call for help and follow the instructions of the emergency services; do not move the person unless necessity requires it.

cards.q: What should be done about severe bleeding while waiting for help?
cards.a: Keep direct pressure on the wound and follow the instructions of 112.

cards.q: What must be kept in mind about your own safety when giving first aid?
cards.a: That the person helping does not put themselves in danger.

cards.q: What should be done after calling 112?
cards.a: Follow the instructions of the emergency operator and give the help that is possible without creating further danger.

cards.q: What is the main aim of the first response at the scene of an accident?
cards.a: To prevent further danger, call for the appropriate help and give assistance according to the situation.

cards.q: The first response at the scene of an accident consists of four main principles that ensure safety and the right assistance. What are they?
cards.a: Secure safety, check the condition, call 112 and give first aid.

cards.q: What information must be given when calling 112?
cards.a: What happened, where the accident is, who is injured and who is calling.

cards.q: May you stop or park in a way that causes danger or unnecessary inconvenience to others?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: On which side of the road may you generally stop or park?
cards.a: On the right.

cards.q: Outside built-up areas, may you stop or park on the left side of the road?
cards.a: Only if it proves impossible to stop or park on the right.

cards.q: Where should you stop or park by the carriageway where possible?
cards.a: At the outermost edge of the carriageway and parallel to it or outside it.

cards.q: May a registered vehicle be parked on a pavement?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided otherwise.

cards.q: May you park on a footpath?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided otherwise.

cards.q: May you park on a cycle path or in a cycle lane?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided otherwise.

cards.q: May you stop or park on a traffic island?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided otherwise.

cards.q: May you stop or park on a grass area?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided otherwise.

cards.q: May you stop or park on a pedestrian crossing?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How close to a pedestrian crossing is stopping or parking prohibited?
cards.a: Within 5 metres of a pedestrian crossing.

cards.q: May you stop or park at a junction?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How close to the nearest edge of the carriageway of the crossing road may you not stop or park at a junction?
cards.a: Within 5 metres.

cards.q: May you stop or park so that a traffic sign cannot be seen?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: May you stop or park so that traffic lights cannot be seen?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: May you stop or park in road tunnels?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided for.

cards.q: May you stop or park under a bridge?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided for.

cards.q: May you stop or park on a bridge?
cards.a: No, unless specifically provided for.

cards.q: May you stop or park at a blind summit where visibility is limited?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: May you stop or park in a bend where visibility is limited?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: May you stop or park in a roundabout?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: May you stop or park by an unbroken centre or dividing line if that makes it difficult to drive into the correct lane?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: If the driver stays in the car, may they stop where stopping is prohibited?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: Do hazard lights allow you to stop or park where it is prohibited?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How should a vehicle door be opened?
cards.a: So that it does not cause danger or unnecessary inconvenience.

cards.q: What is the main function of chevron signs?
cards.a: To give drivers information about the alignment of the road, obstacles or conditions by the road.

cards.q: Why are chevron signs particularly important in the dark?
cards.a: They can help a driver see the direction of the road and the position of obstacles when visibility is poor.

cards.q: Do chevron signs give information about the speed limit?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What are warning signs?
cards.a: Signs that warn of a hazard or of a road that may be difficult to recognise in time.

cards.q: What should a driver do when they see a warning sign?
cards.a: Take extra care and adapt their driving to the conditions the sign warns of.

cards.q: What is a supplementary plate?
cards.a: A sign that gives more detailed information about the main sign.

cards.q: Where is a supplementary plate usually placed?
cards.a: Below the main sign.

cards.q: Can a supplementary plate further define the scope of the main sign?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: What is the purpose of information signs?
cards.a: To give information about roads, routes, places, services or other facilities.

cards.q: What is the purpose of service signs?
cards.a: To show a service or facility that road users can use.

cards.q: What can direction signs show?
cards.a: For example a direction, a route or a destination.

cards.q: Does a direction sign automatically give the driver priority?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What is the purpose of road markings and traffic signs?
cards.a: To control, guide or warn road users.

cards.q: Is it enough to know the colour and shape of a traffic sign without knowing its meaning?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What can a roadworks sign indicate?
cards.a: That works or special conditions are on or by the road.

cards.q: Does a roadworks sign mean a driver may drive faster if they see no workers?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What is important about a sign that warns of a narrowing road?
cards.a: That the driver is prepared for a narrower carriageway and adapts their driving to it.

cards.q: When did the new regulation on traffic signs enter into force?
cards.a: 1 March 2024.

cards.q: What should a driver do when a sign warns of a hazard that they find hard to foresee?
cards.a: Reduce speed according to the conditions and take particular care.

cards.q: What can an information sign tell a driver?
cards.a: For example where a route goes or where a particular service is.

cards.q: Can the meaning of a traffic sign change depending on whether a supplementary plate is present?
cards.a: Yes, a supplementary plate can further define the scope or the conditions.

cards.q: What is the right-hand rule?
cards.a: Where priority is not determined otherwise, you must generally give way to traffic coming from the right.

cards.q: Does the right-hand rule always apply?
cards.a: No. Traffic signs, traffic lights or other rules may determine priority differently.

cards.q: What does it mean to give way?
cards.a: That the driver must give way to traffic that has priority.

cards.q: What does an obligation to stop mean?
cards.a: That the driver must stop and then give way to traffic that has priority.

cards.q: Must you stop at a stop sign even if no car is in sight?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: May you drive over a stop line without stopping if there is no traffic?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What applies if a police officer's directions differ from traffic signs?
cards.a: The police officer's directions must be followed.

cards.q: Do a police officer's directions take precedence over traffic lights?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Do a police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signs?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: What should a driver do if traffic lights are out of order?
cards.a: Follow other applicable rules and signs and take particular care.

cards.q: Does an indicator give a driver priority automatically?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: May a driver rely on another driver giving way just because they have priority?
cards.a: No. A driver must always take account of the conditions and avoid a collision where possible.

cards.q: What should a driver do before driving into a junction?
cards.a: Watch the traffic, the signs and the priority rules.

cards.q: What should a driver do if they see that they cannot get across a junction without blocking traffic travelling across their direction?
cards.a: Not drive into the junction until there is enough space to get across.

cards.q: What is the basic rule for driving in a roundabout?
cards.a: Observe the markings and priority rules and show other road users consideration.

cards.q: Who are unprotected road users?
cards.a: For example pedestrians and cyclists.

cards.q: What should a driver do when approaching a pedestrian crossing?
cards.a: Drive so that they cause a pedestrian no danger or inconvenience and be ready to stop.

cards.q: May a driver stop on a pedestrian crossing?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: When must a driver stop at a pedestrian crossing?
cards.a: If it is necessary to give a pedestrian the chance to cross the carriageway.

cards.q: May you drive past a pedestrian on a crossing without slowing down?
cards.a: Not if it creates danger or inconvenience for the pedestrian.

cards.q: What must a driver particularly keep in mind when children are near the carriageway?
cards.a: That they may step out into the carriageway unexpectedly and that speed must be reduced.

cards.q: Must a driver show children particular care?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Why must a driver show unprotected road users particular care?
cards.a: They are physically unprotected and can suffer serious injuries in a collision.

cards.q: What is reaction distance?
cards.a: The distance a vehicle travels from the moment the driver perceives a hazard until they begin to brake.

cards.q: What is braking distance?
cards.a: The distance from the moment braking starts until the vehicle stops.

cards.q: What is stopping distance?
cards.a: Reaction distance plus braking distance.

cards.q: What happens to reaction distance as speed increases?
cards.a: It increases.

cards.q: Does ice affect braking distance?
cards.a: It increases considerably.

cards.q: Does the condition of the tyres affect grip?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: What happens to braking distance as speed increases?
cards.a: It increases considerably.

cards.q: Is the legal speed limit always a safe speed?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What should a driver do when conditions worsen?
cards.a: Reduce speed and adapt their driving to the conditions.

cards.q: What can rain affect?
cards.a: Grip, visibility and braking distance.

cards.q: What can snow or ice do to braking distance?
cards.a: Lengthen it considerably.

cards.q: Why must you keep enough distance from the vehicle in front?
cards.a: To have enough room to react if it slows down or stops.

cards.q: As a general rule, how long should the gap between vehicles be under the traffic law?
cards.a: Generally not less than three seconds.

cards.q: May a tired driver need a bigger gap?
cards.a: Yes, because their reaction time may be longer.

cards.q: How does fatigue affect driving?
cards.a: It can reduce attention, lengthen reaction time and increase the risk of mistakes.

cards.q: Can you rely on willpower alone to overcome severe fatigue?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How does alcohol affect fitness to drive?
cards.a: It can impair judgement, attention, reactions and coordination.

cards.q: Can medicines affect fitness to drive?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Are all legal medicines safe to drive with?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How can mobile phone use distract from driving?
cards.a: It can take sight, attention or mental capacity away from the driving.

cards.q: What is the safest way to respond to severe fatigue?
cards.a: Stop in a safe place and rest.

cards.q: Can stress affect driving?
cards.a: Yes, it can affect concentration, decision-making and driving behaviour.

cards.q: Why is good concentration important when driving?
cards.a: To be able to follow the traffic, identify hazards and react in time.

cards.q: Does an indicator give a driver priority?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: When should you indicate?
cards.a: When the driver changes direction or position so that other road users need to know.

cards.q: What must a driver do before indicating?
cards.a: Watch the conditions and make sure the intention is safe.

cards.q: Is it enough to indicate without watching the traffic?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: When should you indicate when leaving a roundabout?
cards.a: In good time before leaving the roundabout.

cards.q: Why must the windows be kept clean?
cards.a: To ensure good visibility.

cards.q: Why must the lights be kept clean?
cards.a: To ensure good lighting and visibility.

cards.q: Why is it important to be visible to other road users?
cards.a: So that they can react correctly to the position and movement of the vehicle.

cards.q: Why must a seat belt be used?
cards.a: To reduce the risk of serious injury in a collision or sudden braking.

cards.q: Is it right not to use a seat belt because you are only driving a short distance?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: Why must the head restraint be adjusted correctly?
cards.a: To reduce the risk of neck injuries.

cards.q: Can loose luggage in the passenger compartment be dangerous?
cards.a: Yes. It can be thrown forward in sudden braking or a collision.

cards.q: Why must tyre pressure be correct?
cards.a: It affects grip, handling, braking and tyre wear.

cards.q: Can too low tyre pressure affect handling?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Why must the tyres be checked regularly?
cards.a: To make sure they are in acceptable condition and have enough grip.

cards.q: What should a driver do if they notice a serious fault in the vehicle?
cards.a: Stop in a safe place and deal with the fault.

cards.q: What must be done when a driver leaves a motor vehicle?
cards.a: Stop its engine and secure it so that it cannot roll away on its own or be set in motion by others.

cards.q: If a question contains the word always, what should the student do?
cards.a: Read particularly carefully and check whether any exception makes the statement wrong.

cards.q: If a question contains the word never, what should the student do?
cards.a: Look particularly for whether an exception exists.

cards.q: Is it enough for part of a statement to be correct to mark it true?
cards.a: No. The whole statement must be correct.

cards.q: What is the difference between may and must?
cards.a: May means that something is permitted, while must expresses an obligation.

cards.q: What is most important to do before answering a true/false question?
cards.a: Read the whole statement carefully and look at every word before answering.
